title: A Late Turnaround in Seoul, a Split Rally in New York
body:
For most of Wednesday, it looked as though Korean stocks were heading for another painful session. By 1:34 p.m., the KOSPI had fallen 3.7%, and some traders were already talking about **capitulation** (투매), the point at which exhausted investors sell at any price. What happened next surprised almost everyone. Institutions bought aggressively in the final two hours, and the index managed to **turn around**, closing 0.6% higher at 5,683.80. Such an **abrupt** swing of more than four percentage points is a reminder of how easily a choppy market can **whipsaw** (이리저리 흔들다) traders who act on emotion. Foreign investors, however, dumped about 2.5 trillion won, marking the second **consecutive** day on which they sold more than 1.5 trillion won.

Overnight, Wall Street delivered a rally that looked **broad-based** at first glance. The S&P 500 rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq gained 1.4% after Democrats won control of Congress and oil prices plunged 8.1%, which eased worries about inflation. The VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, dropped 20.3% to 16.61. Chip stocks, though, **lost ground**: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.1% as data center names tumbled. Whereas the S&P 500 has now risen for two straight sessions, chipmakers gave back all of Tuesday's gains in a single night. If that gap persists, the KOSPI's late comeback may prove to be a short break rather than the start of a new trend, since the sector Korea depends on most is still struggling.
ko:
수요일 장 대부분 동안 한국 증시는 또 한 번 고통스러운 하루를 향해 가는 것처럼 보였다. 오후 1시 34분까지 코스피는 3.7% 떨어졌고, 일부 트레이더는 이미 '투매' — 지친 투자자들이 가격 불문하고 파는 지점 — 를 이야기하고 있었다. 그다음에 일어난 일은 거의 모두를 놀라게 했다. 기관이 마지막 두 시간 동안 공격적으로 사들였고, 지수는 방향을 틀어 0.6% 오른 5,683.80에 마감했다. 4%포인트가 넘는 이런 급격한 출렁임은, 변덕스러운 시장이 감정으로 매매하는 사람을 얼마나 쉽게 이리저리 흔들어 놓는지를 다시 일깨워 준다. 그러나 외국인은 약 2.5조 원을 내다 팔았고, 이로써 1.5조 원 넘게 판 날이 이틀 연속이 됐다.

밤사이 월가는 언뜻 보기에 폭넓은 랠리를 보여 줬다. 민주당이 의회 장악에 성공하고 유가가 8.1% 폭락해 인플레이션 걱정이 누그러지자, S&P500은 1.6%, 나스닥은 1.4% 올랐다. 월가의 공포 지수인 VIX는 20.3% 떨어진 16.61을 기록했다. 하지만 반도체주는 밀렸다. 데이터센터 관련주가 급락하면서 필라델피아 반도체지수는 3.1% 하락했다. S&P500은 이제 이틀 연속 올랐지만, 반도체 기업들은 화요일 상승분을 하룻밤 만에 모두 반납했다. 이 격차가 계속된다면, 한국이 가장 크게 기대는 업종이 여전히 고전하고 있으므로 코스피의 막판 반등은 새로운 추세의 시작이 아니라 잠깐의 숨 돌리기로 끝날 수도 있다.

vocab.en_easy: The moment when tired, scared investors give up and sell everything, often near the bottom.
vocab.ex: Some analysts think Wednesday's 3.7% intraday drop was a sign of capitulation, which often comes right before a rebound.

vocab.en_easy: To make someone lose money by moving sharply up and then down (or down and then up).
vocab.ex: I got whipsawed yesterday — I sold at the low and the market bounced an hour later.

vocab.en_easy: Spread across many different areas or groups, not just a few.
vocab.ex: A broad-based rally is healthier than one led by just a handful of big tech stocks.
The weather took an abrupt turn, so we had to cancel our hike and head back down.

vocab.en_easy: Coming one after another without a break.
vocab.ex: I've hit the gym five consecutive days this week, so my legs are really sore.

vocab.en_easy: To change from getting worse to getting better.
vocab.ex: The index turned around in the last two hours and closed in positive territory.

vocab.en_easy: To become weaker or fall behind compared with before or with others.
vocab.ex: While the S&P 500 climbed, chip stocks lost ground for the second time this week.

grammar.point: 관계대명사 what (= the thing that, 명사절 주어 → 단수 동사)
grammar.quote: What happened next surprised almost everyone.
grammar.explain_ko: what 은 선행사를 품은 관계대명사(= the thing that). 'What happened next'가 통째로 문장의 주어(명사절)이고, 명사절 주어는 단수 취급 → surprised(과거)지만 현재형이면 surprises. that 은 선행사가 꼭 앞에 있어야 하므로 'That happened next…'는 불가.
examples: What worries me most is the foreign selling, not the index level.
OPIc: What I like most about staying home on holidays is that I don't have to set an alarm.

grammar.point: 현재완료 vs 과거 (has risen for two straight sessions ↔ gave back … in a single night / Tuesday)
grammar.quote: Whereas the S&P 500 has now risen for two straight sessions, chipmakers gave back all of Tuesday's gains in a single night.
grammar.explain_ko: has risen = 과거부터 '지금까지' 이어지는 흐름(now·for·since 와 잘 어울림). gave back = 끝난 특정 시점(어젯밤 하루)의 사건 → 과거. Tuesday·last night·yesterday 같은 분명한 과거 시점 부사는 현재완료와 같이 못 쓴다(× has given back last night).
examples: Foreign investors have sold Korean stocks for weeks, but they bought chips heavily last spring.
OPIc: I've been to Gangneung three times, but the last time I went, gas prices were crazy high.

tense.sentence: By 1:34 p.m., the KOSPI had fallen 3.7%.
tense.why_ko: '오후 1시 34분'이라는 과거 기준 시점 '까지' 이미 완료된 하락 → by + 과거 시점 + had p.p.

tense.sentence: The S&P 500 has now risen for two straight sessions.
tense.why_ko: 이틀 전부터 지금까지 이어진 연속 상승을 '현재 상태'로 말함 → now·for 와 함께 현재완료.

review.q: After a drop of nearly 20% in a month, the KOSPI looked oversold to some analysts. 밑줄 친 oversold 와 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: priced too high for buyers to take the risk
pushed down further than its true value justifies
traded on unusually thin volume all month
supported by steady demand from foreigners
review.exp_ko: oversold = 팔릴 만큼 팔려 '제값보다 더 많이 떨어진' 상태 → ②. ① 너무 비싸다는 건 반대(overbought) ③ 거래량 얇음은 가격 수준과 무관 ④ 외국인은 계속 팔고 있어 문맥과도 안 맞음.

review.q: ______ the Democrats' win in Congress, the Dow jumped about 1,500 points and oil prices fell sharply.
review.exp_ko: in the wake of = ~의 직후에, ~의 여파로 → 승리 '이후' 급등이라는 시간·인과에 딱 맞음. Ahead of(~을 앞두고)는 이미 확정된 승리와 시점이 맞지 않고, Regardless of(~와 상관없이)·In spite of(~에도 불구하고)는 원인-결과를 끊어 버림.

review.q: I'm still ______ about buying chip stocks after last night's 3% drop — I need a few more days to decide.
review.exp_ko: be on the fence = (결정을 못 하고) 망설이다 → 'need a few more days to decide'와 일치. on edge(초조한)는 감정만 말하고 '결정 보류'를 못 담음, on the house(무료로)·on the rise(오르는 중)는 문맥과 무관.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Although the S&P 500 rallied 1.6%, chip stocks ______ as investors dumped data center names, leaving the semiconductor index 3.1% lower."
quiz.exp_ko: Although(양보) + 지수 3.1% 하락 → 반도체는 '밀렸다' = lost ground. gained traction(탄력을 받다)·found support(지지를 받다)는 상승·방어 의미라 3.1% 하락과 충돌, held their ground(버텼다)도 '하락'을 설명 못 함.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"①What surprised investors most were the speed of the rebound. Foreign investors ②have sold Korean stocks for weeks, yet institutions, ③buying aggressively after 1:34 p.m., lifted the index to a gain that few people ④had expected."
quiz.exp_ko: What 절(What surprised investors most)이 주어 → 명사절 주어는 단수 + 보어 the speed 도 단수 → was 가 맞다. ② for weeks(기간, 지금까지) → 현재완료 ✓ ③ 기관이 '사는' 능동 → 현재분사 buying ✓ ④ 상승(과거)보다 '예상'이 먼저 → 과거완료 had expected ✓.

choices: Foreign selling in Korea is finally over, so the rebound will likely continue.
The U.S. rally will soon spread to Korean chip stocks and lift the KOSPI.
The Democratic win in Congress mainly helped chipmakers rather than other stocks.
A late rebound is no sure sign of a new trend while chip stocks remain weak.
quiz.exp_ko: 글은 '장 막판 반전 + 외국인 매도 지속 + 미국 반도체 약세'를 묶어 '반등이 추세 전환이라 단정 못 한다'로 결론 → ④. ① 외국인은 이틀 연속 1.5조 넘게 팔았음(종료 근거 없음) ② 오히려 미 반도체 3.1% 하락 — 확산 근거 없음 ③ 반도체는 '밀렸다' — 방향이 반대.

choices: 코스피 종가 상승률은 나스닥 상승률의 절반을 넘었다.

talk.topic: From −3.7% to +0.6% — 코스피 막판 대반전, 그런데 밤사이 미국 반도체는 −3.1%
talk.setting_ko: 목요일 아침 출근 엘리베이터. 동료 B는 어제 장중 급락 때 겁나서 팔았고, A는 아무것도 안 하고 버텼다.

dialogue.en: Did you see the KOSPI yesterday? It was down almost four percent after lunch.
dialogue.ko: 어제 코스피 봤어? 점심 지나서 거의 4% 빠졌잖아.

dialogue.en: Don't remind me. I panicked and sold right around the low. Then it turned on a dime and closed up.
dialogue.ko: 말도 마. 겁나서 거의 바닥에서 팔았어. 그러고 나서 순식간에 방향을 틀더니 플러스로 끝났지.

dialogue.en: Ouch. Well, I'd be careful about calling it a bottom. It could just be a head fake.
dialogue.ko: 아이고. 근데 바닥이라고 하긴 조심스러워. 그냥 속임 동작일 수도 있어.

dialogue.en: Why? Wall Street rallied hard overnight, didn't it?
The S&P did, but chip stocks fell three percent. For Korea, we're not out of the woods yet.
dialogue.ko: S&P는 그랬지, 근데 반도체가 3% 빠졌어. 한국 입장에선 아직 고비를 넘긴 게 아니야.

dialogue.en: So should I buy back in this morning?
dialogue.ko: 그럼 오늘 아침에 다시 사야 하나?

dialogue.en: I wouldn't chase a rally right at the open. Let the dust settle for a day or two first.
dialogue.ko: 장 시작하자마자 오르는 거 따라 사진 않을 거야. 하루 이틀 상황이 정리될 때까지 기다려 봐.

dialogue.en: Fair enough. Lesson learned — no more selling in a panic after lunch.
dialogue.ko: 그래, 맞는 말이야. 교훈 얻었다 — 점심 먹고 겁나서 파는 건 이제 그만.

expressions.when_ko: 시장·계획·사람 마음이 갑자기 확 바뀔 때
expressions.ex: The market turned on a dime after 1:30 and closed in the green.

expressions.when_ko: 반등·급락이 진짜 추세가 아니라 일시적 움직임일 수 있다고 말할 때
expressions.ex: That rebound might be a head fake, so I'm not adding more yet.

expressions.ko: 아직 위기를 다 벗어난 건 아니다
expressions.when_ko: 좋아 보이지만 위험이 남아 있을 때 (건강·일·시장 모두)
expressions.ex: My knee feels better, but I'm not out of the woods yet, so no deadlifts this week.

expressions.when_ko: 급등을 보고 뒤늦게 따라 사는 행동을 말릴 때
expressions.ex: I try not to chase a rally on the first day — I wait for a pullback.

expressions.when_ko: 큰 사건 직후 바로 결정하지 말자고 할 때
expressions.ex: Let's let the dust settle after the election before we make any big moves.

your_turn.q_en: Have you ever made a decision in a panic and regretted it later? What happened?
your_turn.hint_ko: 과거 시제로: 상황(언제·무엇) → 겁나서 한 행동 → 결과 → 배운 점. 'turn on a dime', 'let the dust settle' 써 보기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Actually, yes. A few weeks ago the market was falling really fast, and I sold some of my stocks in a panic. Then, out of the blue, prices turned on a dime and went right back up the next day. I felt pretty silly. Now I have a simple rule: when everything looks scary, I let the dust settle for a day before I do anything.

talk.topic: 황금연휴, 멀리 안 가고 집에서 쉬기 — 배달·영화·늦잠 계획 (Background Survey #55 집에서 보내는 휴가)
talk.setting_ko: 금요일 퇴근길, 친구 A가 B에게 연휴 계획을 묻는다. B는 이번엔 어디도 안 가고 집에서 쉴 생각.

dialogue.en: Got any big plans for the long weekend?
Nope. I'm planning a lazy day in — actually, three lazy days in.
dialogue.ko: 아니. 집에서 뒹굴 거야 — 사실 사흘 내내.

dialogue.en: Honestly, that sounds kind of perfect. Traffic's going to be a nightmare anyway.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 완벽하게 들린다. 어차피 길도 엄청 막힐 거고.

dialogue.en: Exactly. I'm just going to veg out on the couch and finally finish that series.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까. 소파에서 멍하니 쉬면서 그 드라마 드디어 끝낼 거야.

dialogue.en: Want company on Saturday? We could grab some fried chicken and watch a movie.
dialogue.ko: 토요일에 같이 있어 줄까? 치킨 시켜서 영화 보자.

dialogue.en: I'm down for that. And the chicken's on me — you got coffee last time.
dialogue.ko: 좋지. 그리고 치킨은 내가 쏠게 — 지난번에 네가 커피 샀잖아.

dialogue.en: Deal. But let's not stay up till 3 a.m. like last time.
dialogue.ko: 콜. 근데 지난번처럼 새벽 3시까지 버티진 말자.

dialogue.en: Ha, no promises. Maybe we'll call it an early night for once.
dialogue.ko: 하하, 장담은 못 해. 이번엔 웬일로 일찍 잘 수도 있지.

expressions.when_ko: 외출 없이 집에서 쉬는 날을 말할 때 (OPIc 집 휴가 단골)
expressions.ex: Rainy Sundays are perfect for a lazy day in with a good movie.

expressions.when_ko: 소파에서 TV 보며 푹 퍼져 쉬는 걸 말할 때
expressions.ex: After leg day, I usually just veg out on the couch for the rest of the evening.
A walk along the river after dinner? I'm down for that.
Dinner's on me tonight — you helped me move last week.

expressions.when_ko: 평소보다 일찍 잠자리에 들거나 모임을 끝낼 때
expressions.ex: I have a race tomorrow morning, so I'm going to call it an early night.

your_turn.q_en: How do you usually spend a holiday when you stay at home? Tell me about a typical day.
your_turn.hint_ko: 현재 시제 루틴: 기상 → 오전 → 점심(배달?) → 오후 → 저녁. 'a lazy day in', 'veg out' 넣고, 마지막에 감정 한 줄.
your_turn.sample_answer: Well, when I stay home on a holiday, I don't set an alarm at all. I usually wake up around ten, make a big cup of coffee, and just veg out on the couch for a while. Around lunchtime, I order in — usually something like jjajangmyeon. In the afternoon, I might go for a short walk in the park near my place, and in the evening I watch a movie or two. To be honest, a lazy day in like that really recharges me.

opic.survey_topic: 목요일 돌발 주제 — 에너지·기름값(물가) (서베이 #56 국내 여행 · #31 주식 투자와 연결)

combo.q_en: I'd like to ask you about energy prices. These days, the prices of gas and electricity seem to go up and down a lot. How do changes in energy prices affect people in your country? Please tell me in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 에너지 가격에 대해 묻고 싶어요. 요즘 기름값과 전기요금이 많이 오르내리는 것 같아요. 에너지 가격 변화가 당신 나라 사람들에게 어떤 영향을 주나요? 최대한 자세히 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(요즘 상황 한 줄: 기름값이 롤러코스터) → 본문 3포인트: ① 운전·출퇴근(주유비·대중교통 갈아탐) ② 집(난방·에어컨 요금, 관리비) ③ 물가 전반(배달비·식당 가격) → 마무리(내 생각 한 줄). 90초~2분. IH/AL 포인트: '사람들' 일반론만 말고 '나·가족' 예시 1개로 구체화, 현재시제 일관, 원인-결과 연결어(so, which means).
combo.model_answer: Okay, energy prices. Well, honestly, it's been a real roller coaster lately. Just this week, oil prices dropped something like eight percent in a single day, but a few months ago gas was so expensive that people were complaining everywhere. So how does it affect people? I think there are three main ways. First, driving. A lot of Koreans commute by car, so when gas prices go up, people feel it right away. Some of my coworkers actually switched to the subway for a while, just to save money. Second, bills at home. In winter, heating costs can be pretty shocking, especially for families living in older apartments. My parents, for example, keep the heater lower and just wear thicker clothes. And third, I mean, prices in general. When energy gets more expensive, delivery fees and restaurant prices tend to go up too, which means everyone ends up paying more, even people who don't drive. So, yeah, energy prices might sound like a boring topic, but they really affect our everyday lives.

key_phrases.en: It's been a real roller coaster lately.
which means everyone ends up paying more
key_phrases.ko: 결국 모두가 더 내게 된다는 뜻이죠

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '기름값 오르면 힘들다'에서 끝남 → IH는 3가지 영향을 First/Second/Third로 나눔 → AL은 각 포인트에 '내 동료·우리 부모님' 실제 예시를 붙이고 'which means~'로 결과까지 연결.

combo.q_en: How have people's ways of saving energy changed compared to the past? What did people do back then, and what do they do differently now?
combo.q_ko: 에너지를 아끼는 방식이 예전과 비교해 어떻게 바뀌었나요? 예전엔 사람들이 어떻게 했고, 지금은 무엇이 달라졌나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(크게 바뀌었다 한 줄) → 과거(used to: 불 끄기, 내복, 멀티탭 뽑기 — 엄마 잔소리) → 현재(스마트 플러그·앱으로 전기 사용량 확인, 에너지 효율 등급 가전, 전기차) → 이유(기술 + 요금 부담) → 마무리(내 습관 변화). IH/AL 포인트: used to / these days 대비 구조로 시제 전환을 분명히, 과거-현재 각각 디테일 2개.
combo.model_answer: Oh, it's changed a lot. Back when I was a kid, saving energy was mostly about, you know, small habits. My mom used to follow me around the house turning off lights, and she'd always say, 'Unplug that, it's eating electricity!' In winter, instead of turning up the heat, we wore long underwear and slept under these super heavy blankets. These days, though, it's much more about technology. A lot of people use smart plugs, so they can turn things off with their phone even when they're not home. Some apps even show you how much electricity you've used this month, which is kind of scary, actually. And when people buy a new fridge or air conditioner, they check the energy efficiency rating first. So why did this change happen? I think it's mainly two things: technology made it easier, and bills got higher, so people pay more attention. Personally, I still turn off the lights like my mom taught me — but now I also check the app. Old habits die hard, I guess.

key_phrases.en: My mom used to follow me around ~ing
instead of turning up the heat
These days, though, it's much more about ~

combo.level_up_ko: IH는 과거/현재를 나열 → AL은 'So why did this change happen?' 하고 스스로 묻고 원인 2개로 답한 뒤, 마지막에 '나는 둘 다 한다'로 과거와 현재를 다시 묶어 마무리.

combo.q_en: Tell me about a time when high gas prices or energy costs affected your plans, such as a trip. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
combo.q_ko: 기름값이나 에너지 비용이 비싸서 계획(예: 여행)에 영향을 받았던 경험을 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떻게 대처했나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·누구와·어디 계획) → 사건(주유소 가격 보고 충격, 왕복 계산) → 대처(KTX로 변경·카풀·일정 축소) → 결과·감정 → 배운 점. 2분. IH/AL 포인트: 과거시제 일관 + 과거완료 1회(had already ~), 대사 인용 1회로 생생하게, 자기수정 1회.
combo.model_answer: Let me think. Oh, I remember one time, it was maybe two summers ago? No, wait, it was last year. My friends and I were planning a road trip to Gangneung, and we had already booked a guesthouse near the beach. The night before we left, I went to fill up the car, and I couldn't believe the price on the sign. I literally said out loud, 'Is this real?' So I did some quick math, and the gas and highway tolls for a round trip were going to cost almost as much as the guesthouse. We had a little emergency group chat that night. In the end, we decided to leave the car at home and take the KTX instead, and then we rented bikes once we got there. Honestly, it turned out even better, because nobody had to drive and we could all relax on the train. Ever since then, I always check gas prices and train tickets before I plan a trip. Lesson learned, I guess.

key_phrases.en: I couldn't believe the price on the sign.
In the end, we decided to ~ instead
It turned out even better, because ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '비싸서 기차 탔다' 한 줄 → IH는 시간 순서(전날 밤→계산→단톡→결정) → AL은 그때 한 말 인용('Is this real?')과 'it turned out even better'로 반전·감정까지 넣어 이야기처럼.

useful.when_ko: 돌발 질문에 바로 답이 안 떠오를 때, 기준을 먼저 세우며 시간 벌기
일반론 다음에 내 경험으로 구체화할 때 (IH→AL 핵심)
두 번째·세 번째 포인트를 자연스럽게 덧붙일 때

useful.en: I've never really thought about it, but ~
useful.when_ko: 낯선 사회 이슈(돌발) 질문을 받았을 때 솔직하게 시작하기
원인 → 결과를 한 문장으로 이어 문단 수준 담화 만들 때

opic.practice_ko: ①번 '에너지 가격' 질문을 타이머 2분으로 녹음 → 들으며 First/Second/Third가 다 나왔는지, 각 포인트에 '내 주변 예시'가 붙었는지 체크. 두 번째 녹음에선 'which means ~'를 최소 2번 넣어 원인-결과를 이어 보기.
